title: Signal-driven fallback queue topology sketch
content:
Context and problem:
- We need a lightweight, observable, and configurable fallback queue topology for ingress controllers to route degraded requests to cheaper/compatible model variants or to queued retry lanes.
- Goals: predictable tail latency isolation, clear accounting, easy policy expression, and minimal cross-team coupling.
- Constraints: must work for hosted and dedicated modes; prefer config-driven rules (console + API) so product can tune without deploys.

High-level idea (signal-driven fallback):
- Ingress nodes export compact health signals: {rps, avg_ms, p95_ms, queue_depth, model_variant_util}% per route and per model shard.
- A central decision-plane (logical, can be local cache in each region) compiles "fallback rules" that map signals -> actions.
- Actions: route_to_variant, enqueue_in_fallback_queue, shed_cheap, return_503-with-backoff, apply-rate-limit, annotate-telemetry.

Topology variants:
1) Local-per-ingress fallback (fastest):
   - Each ingress maintains local queues and a tiny policy engine.
   - Pros: lowest added latency, decoupled. Cons: harder to maintain global fairness and cross-node capacity accounting.

2) Regional-fallback-queue (hybrid):
   - Ingress nodes forward overflow to regional queue service (stateless workers consume and dispatch to backing pools).
   - Pros: centralizes accounting, easier to throttle. Cons: extra hop, requires regional dispatch capacity.

3) Global-control with local enforcement (recommended default):
   - Central controller publishes lane configs and admission thresholds; ingress enforces locally and uses short-lived tickets to claim global slots when needed.
   - Balances global fairness + local latency.

ASCII diagram (global-control variant):

  [ingress-A] --health-> [controller] <-health-- [ingress-B]
        | enqueue?
        v
  [local-queue-A] --ticket-request--> [controller] --grant--> [dispatch-pool]

Components and APIs (rough):
- Signal v1 (sent every 500ms):
  POST /internal/telemetry/signal
  body: {"node_id":"ingress-A","route":"/v1/generate","rps":12.3,"p95_ms":234,"queue_depth":6,"variants":{"gpt-neo-8b":0.72}}

- Fallback rules (controller) shape (expressive minimal DSL):
  {
    "rule_id": "fallback-high-latency-1",
    "match": {"route":"/v1/generate","p95_ms":">200"},
    "action": {"type":"route_to_variant","variant":"gpt-neo-4b-quant","ttl_sec":300},
    "priority": 10
  }

  Note: JSON above is an example; we should support time windows and STAN-style epochs for stable decisions.

- Ticket API for claiming dispatch slots:
  POST /internal/fallback/ticket/request {"node_id":"ingress-A","lane":"best-effort","want":3}
  -> returns {"granted":1, "expires_at":"2026-03-01T12:03:00Z", "dispatch_id":"d-xyz"}

Telemetry and accounting:
- Each enqueue/dequeue emits events: fallback.enqueue, fallback.dequeue, fallback.expire with tags: node, route, lane, ticket_id.
- Cost allocation: attach original request owner metadata through ticket lifecycle to bill correct tenant.

Policy language thoughts (sketchy):
- match on metrics and topological tags (region, node-type, customer-tier)
- actions chainable: e.g., route_to_variant + enqueue_in_fallback_queue(before=30s)
- support emergency overrides: global panic rule that routes to 503 for non-SLA customers

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Where to keep long-tail state? naive local queues risk OOM on large traffic bursts. regional queue mitigates but introduces network hops.
- Ticket granularity: per-request vs per-slot. per-request has precise accounting but more messaging.
- How to test deterministic replay of signals for canary rules? need a signal-replay harness.
- How to express multi-variant hedging (try fast small model, if > Xms then fallback to bigger model) without duplicating requests? hedging introduces cost.

Prototype plan (short):
- Phase 0: implement signal emitter + controller proto that accepts signals and stores sliding-window aggregated metrics. (2w)
- Phase 1: implement simple rule compiler that can produce binary decisions; local enforcement in ingress simulator; add telemetry events. (3w)
- Phase 2: add ticketing endpoint and regional queue prototype; run synthetic overload sims; collect cost vs latency curves. (4w)

Acceptance criteria (for initial MVP):
- Ingress can be configured with controller URL and fallback rules via config file.
- Under synthetic overload, requests beyond threshold are either routed to cheaper variants or enqueued, and we can observe correct telemetry counts and ticket lifecycle.
- No p50 regression for baseline traffic.

Notes to self / TODOs: 
- Wire up to /console feature toggle as a beta.
- Add tests for ticket expiry race (double-grant).
- Design fallback queue persistence model (redis vs local LRU with backpressure).
- Check legal/CS concerns for cross-tenant queueing (data residency?).

References / inspiration:
- previous doc: ingress-circuit-breaker-sketchbook (see mental overlap)
- backlog ticket: JIRA-ENG-1287 (linked)

Rough config example (ingress):
  fallback_controller: https://controller.rw.internal
  signal_interval_ms: 500
  fallback_lanes:
    - name: "premium"
      priority: 1
      max_queue_depth: 1000
    - name: "best-effort"
      priority: 5
      max_queue_depth: 5000

Final notes: keep this as exploratory. Next step: pair with Jordan Liu for the ticket API sketch and run a small sim to measure p99 amplification.

-- end of sketch (brain dump)
